title: Inferring Regular Languages in Polynomial Updated Time
venue: Pattern Recognition and Image Analysis, Series in Machine Perception and Artificial Intelligence, vol.1, World Scientific,1992,pp.49–61
relevance: Introduces the RPNI passive state-merging context for inferring a DFA consistent with positive and negative examples; this project instead reasons over ownership partitions and does not learn component DFAs.
title_alias: Commonly cited as Inferring regular languages in polynomial update time
primary_verification: Publisher search result for DOI10.1142/9789812797902_0004 confirms title, authors and volume; direct fetch returned403. Earlier unrelated volume assertion removed.

title: Language identification in the limit
relevance: Foundational identification-in-the-limit results distinguish positive-only text from labeled informants and motivate why finite observations require explicit assumptions and coverage conditions; it is not a direct theorem about this partition solver.

title: Learning Regular Sets from Queries and Counterexamples
primary_source: Author's original paper PDF hosted by University of Illinois Chicago; DOI 10.1016/0890-5401(87)90052-6
relevance: Defines the active teacher/query setting for regular-language learning, useful as a contrast with the static labeled sample here; the paper's oracle access is not assumed by this project.

title: Decomposing Permutation Automata
primary_source: Dagstuhl LIPIcs proceedings page and paper
relevance: Studies decomposition of a given DFA language into intersections of smaller DFA languages, a neighboring compositionality problem; its input, decomposition target, and hypotheses differ from inferring a disjoint alphabet partition from positive/negative words.
